title: The session list is rendered by the host from the list projection and the workspace ledger; every view option and order is host state
Reading state is a stored position per person combined with a completion folded from the log, and a turn is acknowledged when its end is drawn in a visible page
The side panel is a host-stored list of side tabs in at most two panes, selected by URL; there is no dock engine, no floating panel and no operation log
The embedded web browser tab is not built, and nothing replaces it in the side panel
Documents are previewed by host-side renderers; PDF is the one island; office files need the installed LibreOffice and say so when it is missing
The files tree is drawn one level per request, its state belongs to the session on the host, and a directory is watched only while it is on a page
Terminal tabs are the host's roster, drawn by a framed island; the newest viewer types; the host never opens a person's panel by itself
One server-rendered directory picker; the host opens workspace directories only; open-with and show-file-location for files are not built
The session panel and the More menus are regions with stored preferences, built from the browser's own popover and CSS
A person sees every workspace and session, live, and can start a new session
A person can find, rename, fork, pin, reorder, archive and delete sessions, and manage workspaces
Rows show who is waiting, what is running and what is unread, and reminders survive a restart
A side panel where features open tabs beside the conversation
A person can browse and search the files of a session's workspace
A person can preview text, Markdown, images, PDF, spreadsheets, office documents and HTML files
A person has terminals beside the conversation that fit, reconnect and can be watched from two windows
A person can choose a directory of the host machine and add it as a workspace, from any browser
Session facts, open-in and entry choices have one place each
Golden session lists for every grouping, sort mode and archive filter
A change replaces only the affected list regions and the baseline is complete and filtered
The new-session form names workspace, preset and request id; view options are per principal and in the first response
Rename, archive with stop, delete and reorder dialogs and forms follow the routes and the access helper
Search results: metadata then content, capped, with event links and a plain state when the index is off
Reading record transitions and row status precedence
Reading records are durable, shared across connections, per principal, and deleted with their session
Side tab kinds: registration, claim order, no kind for web addresses, unload and reveal
Side state is stored per principal and session, validated, selected by URL and equal in page and fragment
The files tree lists lazily, marks a cut level, watches only open directories and reveals the current file
File search preferences per workspace root, path highlighting and failure lines
Renderer choice, line windows, and Markdown previews under the model-output rules
Spreadsheet table goldens, bounds before allocation and escaped workbook strings
Office previews with a fake office service: available, unavailable, status change, legacy spreadsheet, timeout
The HTML preview document is filtered and served with its own policy; the interactive mode is bounded
Terminal roster, frame document, fallback and close confirmation
Directory picker: host-written paths, host-side filters, create errors and owner-only access
Session panel sections, open-in gating, hidden entries and the creator action
Catalogue completeness in English and Chinese, no literal product text, unique shortcut commands
Two browser tabs and a second process keep one session list
Files and previews in a real browser, with and without LibreOffice
A terminal fits, reconnects and is shared by two windows
Choosing a directory and open-in, from the host machine and from another machine
A hostile file cannot leave its preview

reason: The left column (brand, New Session, entry rows with a More menu, the seat for the workspace browser, the collapsed rail and the narrow-screen drawer, packages/client/ui-sidebar/README.md:14, :32, :42) becomes one host-rendered contribution to the shell's navigation region. Seats become regions, the JavaScript wheel splitting is replaced by a single scroller, and the Electron title-bar and macOS traffic-light layouts have no counterpart because there is no desktop window.

Grouped, tree and flat session lists, sort modes, search, rename, fork, pin, archive with a stop dialog, and workspace add and delete (packages/client/ui-workspace/README.md:14, :40, :48, :58, :68) are kept as host-rendered fragments over the list projection, the workspace ledger and the session and workspace routes. The browser-side catalog, the browser-stored session order, retained recent views and drag-and-drop are not carried; session deletion is added.

The package adapts the session catalog to React hooks and session-scoped slots and holds the highest-precedence pending interaction per session (packages/client/ui-session/README.md:11-13). The hooks and slots have no counterpart in a server-rendered UI; the one rule it owns, which pending interaction a row shows, is folded into the row status that the reading service composes on the host, and its access hooks are the shell's access helper.

A host service that keeps reading state outside the session log and shares it with every browser (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:12, :59-61) is kept as reading.Service. Changed: records are stored per principal and session instead of held in memory, completion is read from the list summary folded from the log, and explicit marks carry a revision. The client half that merged three sources into a status table becomes one host function.

A header toggle and a panel of contributed sections that docks in the transcript gutter or opens as an overlay (packages/client/ui-session-panel/README.md:12, :32-34, :41) are kept as a host-rendered fragment with regions for sections, indicators and environment rows. The resize observer, the dock probe and the Escape handling in script are replaced by the browser's popover attribute and a stylesheet container rule.

The per-session side surface, its tab-type registry with bands and address patterns, and the navigation service (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:12, :85-95) are kept as side.Surface: kinds registered as effects, a stored tab list per person and session, selection in the URL. The dock engine, floating panels, the recorded operation sequence and the localStorage layout are not built; a pop-out page replaces floating.

The files page and the workspace tree listed one level at a time, with host-side name search and exclusion rules (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:12, :59, :80-84), are kept as the files kind over the workspace-file routes. Tree state moves from a per-pane client store to the session's side state on the host, watches become stream interests, and search preferences move from browser storage to host preferences per workspace root.

The fallback file tab with a renderer registry (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:12, :37) is kept as the preview kind and preview.Renderers. Text, Markdown, code, images and spreadsheets are rendered by the host; PDF stays a JavaScript island on vendored pdf.js; Word and PowerPoint files go through the office service; HTML is a filtered document in a sandboxed frame. The browser-side spreadsheet grid and parsers and the client conversion cache are not built.

An interactive shell tab drawn by xterm.js over the host's terminal service, with a shell picker, rename, reconnect, take control and agent terminals marked as such (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md:12, :32-40), is kept. The widget becomes a framed island fed by the one WebSocket; the tab list is the host's roster instead of a saved layout, and an agent terminal marks the toggle instead of expanding the panel.

The package shows a web page inside a side tab, as a sandboxed iframe on the web and an Electron webview on the desktop (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:12, :63). The owner dropped the embedded browser pane: links open in the user's own browser. The page policy also allows frames of the host's origin only. No screenshot stream of the agent's browser is added in its place.

The in-page dialog that lists, navigates and creates directories of the host machine (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-browse/README.md:12, :32) is kept as a host-rendered dialog over the host's directory browser. The Miller-column React view and client-side hidden filtering are replaced by one listed level per request with the filter applied on the host.

A renderless occupant that opens the operating system's folder chooser on the host's display or through the Electron preload bridge (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-native/README.md:12, :30). There is no desktop application, a chooser on the host's display assumes the person sits there, and the Windows dialog needs native code that a pure-Go binary cannot carry. The server-rendered picker is the only way to choose a directory.

Open-in menus for a session's directory (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:12, :36) are kept as menu items that post to the host's open-path route and are drawn only where that route exists, which is for a local owner. The file half (open with an associated application, show file location, association caching, :42-44) is not built, because the host opens workspace directories only; a file is previewed, popped out, downloaded or its path copied.

The shared content of three More menus, with hidden entries, Browse other plugins and Create your plugin (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:14, :31-33), is kept for the navigation column and the side panel's start page as host-rendered menus over stored hidden lists. Slot registration into three regions is React-specific; the conversation view's own menu belongs to the conversation area.

The schema carries spreadsheet limits (excel.maxBytes 16 MiB, maxCells 250000, timeoutMs 15000) and the browser-side office conversion cache limits (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:83-87, :102-106). The Go struct preview.Config keeps the spreadsheet bounds as SheetMaxBytes, SheetMaxCells and SheetTimeout and adds page size, a Markdown bound and the HTML preview limits. The office cache fields have no counterpart because the conversion cache belongs to the host's office service, and nothing is synced to a browser.

ctx.sessionStatus stores the owner's reading acknowledgements and manual unread marks outside session history and streams them to clients (docs/capability-seams.md:741). It becomes the service key reading.Key with interface reading.Service (Status, Seen, Mark). The follow stream is replaced by the shell state of the event stream, and records are stored per principal instead of kept in a process map.

The note separates watching a file (a shared observation by address) from reading it (bounded host reads), and takes the session only from the file address (note lines 13-17). Both rules stand. The host half is the workspace-file routes, where the session is a path segment; observation is no longer a client resource hook but an interest of the browser tab that replaces the preview region or flags it as changed. Renderer registration by extension is kept on the host. The first verdict stands.

The note gives each view or operation its own counted reference to a client session object and forbids a global current session (note lines 7-17). With no session objects in the browser there is nothing to count: a page names its session in the URL, a fragment route binds it as a path parameter, and the one UI status read interface the note asks for is reading.Status on the host. The rule that no global current session exists is kept. The first verdict stands.

The note keeps a tab's DOM ancestors connected through session switches, pane moves and floating, because Electron's webview resets its guest when detached (note lines 9-13). The webview and the browser tab are gone. The goal that remains, that switching does not lose a live thing, is met without DOM retention: the terminal's screen lives in the host emulator and is redrawn from a snapshot, and a preview restores its position from the per-tab store. The first verdict's reference to a system webview no longer applies.

Each region keeps its own list of hidden entries and draws its own More menu, and one package supplies the shared menu content (note lines 15-25). The feature stands for the navigation column and the start page: each owner filters its entries by a stored host preference, so the choice survives a reload, which the shipped package does not achieve. Sharing the menu content through three slot registrations is React-specific. The first verdict stands.

New Session reuses the workspace's first blank session so that an unsent draft is not lost, and a request that names a preset skips a blank that lists another preset (note lines 17-22). The rule is kept and moves from the client's navigation code into the host's create route, which checks the blank under its lease; this area's form sends the workspace, the preset and a request id. The first verdict stands.

Tree state is kept per pane because the dock mounts only the selected tab's body, hidden trees hold no host watch, and the plugin that mounts the tree decides where a file opens (note lines 15-33). In the Go design the expansion set belongs to the session's side state on the host, so it survives any redraw and is the same in every browser tab; a watch is a stream interest that exists only while the directory is on a page; where a file opens is decided by the side surface's Open call. The first verdict left the placement of the state to this area.

The note replaces a single-purpose detail panel with a per-session docking surface (splits, tabs, floats, an undoable operation sequence) so that any feature can open content beside the conversation (note lines 9-15). The shared surface and its tab-type registry are kept. The first verdict asked this area to choose between an island for the layout and a server-driven model: the choice is server-driven, with at most two panes, selection in the URL and a pop-out page instead of floats; the engine and the log, whose undo was never exposed (note line 79), are not built.

Spreadsheets are parsed in the browser so that the preview shows formulas with saved results and does not depend on the office engine, and an unsupported drawing must not block the cells (note lines 9-15). The requirements are kept. The first verdict asked this area to choose where to parse: the host parses with the library the spreadsheet specification verified and renders tables, legacy xls goes through the office engine, and no grid widget ships.

The note adds a browser side tab as a sandboxed iframe with a strict address parser (note lines 13-15). The first verdict was ported, on the ground that an iframe is plain HTML. It is overruled: the owner dropped the embedded browser pane, the page policy allows only frames of the host's own origin, and the note itself records that many sites refuse embedding and that an escaped popup can navigate the application (note line 71). Links open in the user's browser.

The host keeps one reading record per session and streams it to every client so that reminders agree, including for turns that end while no client is connected, and reading never enters the log or the model's history (note lines 9-11). Kept. The first verdict asked whether in-memory is still enough: it is not, because several processes share one home and the note's own consequence is that a restart forgets every reminder (note line 55). The record is stored per principal, and completion comes from the log's list summary.

Session facts get one floating panel that docks only while the gutter beside the transcript has room and is otherwise a temporary overlay (note lines 11-13, 46). The goal is kept. The first verdict expected a small script for the overlay's focus, Escape and outside-press behaviour; this area uses the browser's popover attribute for those and a stylesheet container rule for docking, so no script is written. The inference about docking a closed popover needs a browser check and has a stated fallback.

The sidebar scrollbar thumb stays for 500 ms after the pointer leaves and fades over 200 ms through a CSS transition on a registered custom property, with no JavaScript timer (note lines 11-13). The technique is independent of React and is exactly what a server-rendered page wants; the navigation column's style sheet carries the same rule. Whether the pointer is inside the column is expressed with a hover selector, since the column has one scroller. The first verdict stands.

The picker still lists and creates directories only: no search, no multi-select, no rename or delete (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-browse/README.md:78). A prefix filter of the listed level is kept as a query parameter applied on the host.
justification: The dialog's job is to return one directory path. The host's directory browser offers exactly two operations, list one level and create one child, and adding rename or delete would give a web page a way to change the host's filesystem outside the tool pipeline and the file fence. Search would be a recursive walk of the whole machine.

reason: Upstream always sends hidden entries and hides them in the browser (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-browse/README.md:79). The Go picker passes the show-hidden choice as a query parameter and the host leaves hidden entries out of the fragment it renders, using the host's own hidden rule, which on Windows includes the hidden file attribute.

An open operating-system chooser cannot be closed from the browser because the wire has no per-request abort (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-native/README.md:80). No chooser is opened on the host: the picker is a dialog in the page, closed by the page, and each of its requests ends with the request context.

The native surface works only for local carriers, and remote or in-process deployments must be composed with the browse surface (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-native/README.md:81). There is one surface, rendered by the host, which works the same from a local browser, a forwarded port and another machine, so no composition choice exists.

On Linux without zenity or kdialog the host silently selects the browse surface even on the desktop (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-native/README.md:82). No helper program is looked for and nothing is selected at boot: the server-rendered picker is the only surface on every platform.

Only the left sidebar offers pin controls and the choice lives in memory, so a plugin reload restores every entry (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:68). The navigation column and the side panel's start page each store their hidden entries as a host preference per principal, rendered into the first response, so the choice survives a reload, a restart and a second browser.

The bullet says that pin values an older upstream client wrote to localStorage are neither read nor written (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:69). It exists only because of an earlier format of the upstream browser client. The Go UI has no earlier format and does not read upstream browser storage, because it is not a compatible port.

Create your plugin does not check that the Creator preset exists, so the action can fail after the click (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:70). The host renders the menu, so it asks the preset registry first and draws the row only when the preset exists and a workspace can be resolved; a failure of the create route afterwards is an ordinary error answer in the notice area.

The More menus offer no sorting: entries appear in registration order (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:71). In the Go design entries appear in the order their contributions declare, and the user can hide them but not reorder them. The estimated tab split of the conversation header is that area's concern.
justification: A user-defined order needs a second stored list per region and a reorder control for a handful of links. The contribution order is chosen by the product and stays stable when a component loads or unloads, which a stored order would have to reconcile.

reason: The right-sidebar More menu needs a selected session and appears on its start page (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:72). That is unchanged: the side panel exists only on a session page. The navigation column's menu is available on every page.
justification: Every side tab kind this area ships (files, preview, terminal) is reached through a session, because the file and terminal routes are access-controlled per session. A side panel without a session would have nothing it is allowed to show.

reason: The menus do not list plugins; a browsing action opens the Plugins page (packages/client/ui-entry-customization/README.md:73). The Go menus do the same with a link, drawn when the settings area's plugins page is registered.
justification: What is installed, what it asked for and what it was granted is shown in one place, the plugins page. Plugins are local directories the operator placed and there is no discovery, so a second list in a menu would add nothing a person can act on there.

reason: An application added to the host catalog stays invisible until both client dictionaries gain a matching label (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:96). The host renders the menu: a built-in entry takes its label from the message catalogue, and an operator-defined entry from a config layer shows the name the operator gave it, which is data and is shown as written. No entry is hidden for lack of a translation.

Application availability is read once per page, so a newly installed application appears only after a reload and a host restart (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:97). The menu is rendered from the host's catalog each time it is opened, and the host resolves launchers again on demand after a refresh interval, so neither a reload nor a restart is needed.

File associations are cached per file type for the page, so one file's answer is shown for another (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:98). The Go design never hands a file to an application on the host, so it asks for no file association and caches none. A file is previewed in the side panel, popped out, downloaded or its path copied.

A file type's first open-with menu waits up to 300 ms for the host's association answer (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:99). There is no association query: file menus hold only actions the host can render at once (open in side panel, open in new window, download, copy path).

Opening another file menu cancels the previous menu's unanswered association query (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:100). With no association queries there is no background refresh to cancel.

The reveal action has one label for every platform because the client does not know which file manager the host runs (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:101). The reveal action is not built: the host opens workspace directories in catalog applications only and never reveals a file, so no label is needed.

Delivery cards keep their own way of opening declared files instead of the shared file controls (packages/client/ui-open-in-app/README.md:102). In the Go design there is one way to show a file from anywhere: a link built by side.Surface.Href that opens the preview kind, so a delivered file and a file in the tree open the same way and no second opener exists.

With the default transcript width the page must be about 1608 px wide for the panel to dock; narrower pages get the overlay (packages/client/ui-session-panel/README.md:120). The Go panel follows the same rule: it docks only when the gutter beside the transcript has room.
justification: Docking by moving the transcript column aside takes width from the conversation, which is what the panel was introduced to avoid. Whether the layout should trade that width is a decision of the layout area; until it is made the overlay is the honest behaviour on a laptop.

reason: The client has no per-session fact for the local machine, an SSH host or the sandbox mode, so the Environment section names only the working folder (packages/client/ui-session-panel/README.md:121). The host renders the section and knows all three: it adds rows for the execution world and the sandbox mode beside the working folder.

Every live section shows; hiding or reordering sections from the panel is not offered (packages/client/ui-session-panel/README.md:122). Unchanged: sections appear in contribution order and a section with nothing to show draws nothing.
justification: The panel holds a few sections, each of which hides itself when empty. A per-user section list would need a stored preference and a control inside a small panel, for little gain; the hidden-entry preference is spent on the navigation column and the start page, where the lists are longer.

reason: The toggle in the trajectory view cannot select the chat view, because the conversation package exposes no view selection to plugins (packages/client/ui-session-panel/README.md:123). Views are URLs in the Go UI, so on a view that does not show the panel the toggle is an ordinary link to the session's chat view, where the panel is.

A session shown in the main body and in an embedded conversation shows its overlay in both, because every chat view occurrence renders the aside (packages/client/ui-session-panel/README.md:124). The panel is one element with one id on the session page's main view; a conversation embedded in a side tab does not declare the panel region.

Concurrent explicit marks have last-processed semantics with no revision comparison, so a delayed read action can clear a newer manual unread mark (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:95). Each record has a revision; the mark form carries the revision it was rendered at, and a stale one is refused with the row re-rendered. Automatic acknowledgement still never clears a manual mark.

Separate host processes do not synchronize reading state (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:96). Records live in a table of the shared harness home, and a process sees another process's write at the next revision refresh, so every dsh process on one home shows the same reminders. Machines with separate homes still do not synchronize, which is the scope of a home.

A host restart or plugin reload resets all reading state, forgets failed outcomes, and can leave reading commands disabled until a page reload (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:97). The read position and the manual mark are stored, and the last completed turn and its outcome come from the list summary folded from the log, so nothing is lost on restart. There is no client reading stream that can end in a terminal error: a mark is an ordinary form post.

Only web profiles run the reading service, so a turn finished under another profile leaves no completion (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:98). Completion is no longer observed by a web-only service: it is a field of the list summary that every profile folds from the log, so a turn that ended under a command-line run shows as unread when the web UI next lists the session.

A terminal stream or protocol failure disables reading commands until the page reloads (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:99). The page holds no reading stream of its own: marks are requests and reminders arrive as replacements of list regions on the tab's one event stream, which reconnects by itself. A failed request leaves the previous mark and shows the error; the next request works.

Records of sessions unloaded from memory remain until the service stops, because no session deletion lifecycle exists (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:100). Sessions can be deleted in the Go design, and the reading component deletes a session's records when it is. Nothing is held per unloaded session in memory. Archived sessions still read as read and offer no mark, which is kept as a rule.

Acknowledgement can run while a settings or auxiliary panel covers the conversation, because main-view retention does not distinguish them (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:101). Acknowledgement is sent by the end-of-turn element itself when the browser draws it in a visible page. Settings and other panels are separate pages, so while one is shown the conversation's elements are not in the document and nothing is acknowledged.

There are no message counts and no read receipts for other people; the state is the owner's and viewers of a shared session cannot read or change it (packages/client/ui-session-status/README.md:102). The Go record is keyed by principal, so a non-owner gets reminders of their own, which is new; counts and receipts for others are still not offered.
justification: A reminder answers one question for one person: did something finish that I have not looked at. Showing one person what another has read is a different feature with its own privacy question, and no outcome asks for it.

reason: Pending interactions are process-local projections in the browser, so the owning remote must replay an outstanding request after a reconnect (packages/client/ui-session/README.md:48). The browser keeps no projection: the pending interaction of each session is read from the host's interaction registry when a row is rendered, and the interaction state of the event stream is complete on every connect.

Many sites refuse iframe embedding or need capabilities the sandbox withholds, and disabling the sandbox lets the framed page navigate the application (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:104). The browser tab kind is not built, so no foreign page is framed and there is no sandbox to disable. Links open in the user's own browser.

On the web a popup that escapes the sandbox keeps its opener and can navigate the top-level application (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:105). No page is framed, and every link the UI writes carries a fixed noopener relation, so a page opened from the product has no handle on it.

A later iframe load shows that navigation happened but not the new cross-origin address, so Back and Forward become unavailable (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:106). The limit belongs to framing a foreign page; with the tab kind not built, history is the user's own browser's.

Browsers conceal many iframe failures, so the load-failure notice is best effort (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:107). No foreign page is loaded inside the product, so there is no failure to detect; the user's browser reports its own.

A browser tab's saved title and address survive reloads but page memory, forms and history do not, and saved addresses can hold sensitive query values (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:108). No browser tab state exists and no visited address is stored by the harness.

Local files are rejected by the browser tab and remain owned by document preview (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:109). With no browser tab there is nothing to reject: the side panel's registry has no kind that claims a web address, and a file address is claimed by the preview kind.

The desktop shares storage partitions by workspace directory, loses cookies on restart and denies guest permissions, and its host-address filter is not a private-network firewall (packages/client/ui-sidebar-browser/README.md:110). There is no desktop application and no guest browser, so there are no partitions, leases or filters to maintain.

The viewers offer no editing and no shared search, a directory address fails, and unknown extensions use the plain-text reader (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:146). Unchanged in substance. One gain: host-rendered text and tables are ordinary page content, so the browser's own find works on what is loaded.
justification: The side panel is a read-only view by decision: writing a file is the agent's work through the guarded tool pipeline, or the person's own editor and terminal. An editor in the page would be a second, unguarded way to change the workspace. Plain text as the fallback for unknown types is the intended behaviour.

reason: The preview launches no native Office editor and downloads no engine, binary doc and ppt files report no missing fonts, and fidelity belongs to the LibreOffice provider (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:147). Unchanged: conversion is done by the LibreOffice the operator installed, and what it reports is what can be shown.
justification: The owner decided that office documents use an operator-installed LibreOffice and that nothing is bundled or downloaded. Fidelity and font diagnostics are properties of that program and its version, which the preview reports but cannot improve. The host never opens a file in a native application.

reason: Deep source lines require loading every preceding page, and PDF, HTML and images need the complete file inside the host cap (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:148). The text route takes a line parameter, so a preview opens a window around any line without the lines before it. Images and PDFs are fetched from the byte route, which supports ranges, so the PDF island need not hold the file whole. An HTML file is still filtered as one bounded document.

Each PDF page bitmap is capped at 16,777,216 pixels, so very large pages or high zoom on dense displays render below device resolution (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:149). The island keeps the same cap, passed to it as an attribute.
justification: The cap bounds the memory one page can take in the browser and is a stated requirement of the PDF library specification. Removing it would let one document exhaust a tab.

reason: PDF, HTML and image previews can return to the top when their renderer remounts (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:150). Narrowed: host-rendered previews and images keep their scroll position through the per-tab store, and the PDF island stores its page and zoom there. What remains is scrolling inside the sandboxed HTML frame, which the page cannot read or set.
justification: The HTML preview runs in a frame without same-origin access so that the file cannot reach the application. The same isolation hides the frame's scroll position from the page; weakening it to restore a scroll offset would trade a security control for a convenience.

reason: For a scripted HTML preview only directly referenced classic js and css files are packed, and no file-read bridge is exposed to the frame (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:151). The Go interactive mode packs the same finite set on the host under the same three bounds.
justification: The frame has no same-origin access and its requests carry no credential, so it cannot fetch workspace files itself; that is the point of the sandbox. A bridge that reads files for the frame would give an untrusted document a channel to the workspace. The preview is for generated static pages, not for running an application.

reason: Every scroll event writes its offset to a client store, and memoized line blocks keep React from re-rendering (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:152). The limit exists only because of the React store and its render cycle. The Go UI has no client store: the first-party script keeps scroll positions in the per-tab store without rendering anything.

A failed PDF chunk load needs a page reload because React caches a rejected lazy import (packages/client/ui-sidebar-documentpreview/README.md:153). The PDF viewer is an island whose module the first-party script imports when the element appears and imports again the next time it appears after a failure; until then the element shows its fallback, a download link.

The files view only lists: no content search, artifact filter, drag-and-drop or rename (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:113). Unchanged: the tree lists and opens, and search matches names and relative paths.
justification: The view is read-only by decision, for the reason given for the preview: a rename or a drop from a web page would change the workspace outside the tool pipeline. Content search across a workspace is a tool the agent has; offering it to a person needs a bounded search route and a result view that no area has specified.

reason: A hidden current file is left out of the tree while hidden entries are off, so its row cannot be marked or scrolled to (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:114). The host renders the tree and always includes the current file's row and its ancestors, marked as hidden entries, whatever the toggle says.

On Windows the tree hides only dot-names while the host search also hides entries with the hidden attribute, so an entry can be drawn but not found (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:115). One rule is applied on the host for both: a dot prefix or the Windows hidden attribute. It depends on the listing carrying a hidden flag per entry, which this area asks of the workspace-file routes.

A query containing a slash highlights nothing, because each name is highlighted on its own (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:116). The host renders search results as relative paths and highlights the match on the path it matched, so a query that spans a separator is marked.

An exclusion rule may not contain glob characters, so a literal path such as a directory named with square brackets cannot be excluded (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:117). A rule is defined as a literal name or a literal relative path and is never interpreted as a pattern, so any character is allowed. It depends on the search route taking literal exclusions, which this area asks of the workspace-file routes.

Search preferences are read from browser storage once per tab and written back whole, so one tab overwrites another's changes (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:118). The preferences are host state per principal and workspace root, changed by a request and rendered into every response, so tabs and browsers cannot diverge.
The tree is rooted at the session's workspace root and cannot browse above it; the host refuses paths outside the root anyway (packages/client/ui-sidebar-files/README.md:119). Unchanged.
justification: The workspace-file routes keep listing, search and watching inside the workspace by decision, so that a session's file view is scoped to its project. A single named file outside the root can still be previewed when the session's filesystem backend allows the read.

reason: The layout is saved in the browser's localStorage and does not synchronize between devices (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:151). The side tabs of a session and their placement are stored by the host per principal, so every browser and device of that person shows the same tabs; pane sizes are a preference per platform class.
State is keyed by session id, so the page with no session shows nothing on the right (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:152). Unchanged: the side panel exists on session pages only.
justification: Files, previews and terminals are reached through a session, because their routes are access-controlled per session and the tree's root is a session's directory. Without a session there is no directory and no access rule to draw anything under.

reason: The content tree uses a fixed stacking layer and floating panels reorder inside it without rising above menus (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:153). There are no floating panels and no hand-numbered layers: the side panel is a column of the page, and menus, dialogs and the session panel overlay use the browser's top layer.

A session that leaves the catalog does not retire its retained view; tab lifetimes and plugin teardown own the release (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:154). Nothing is retained in the browser per session. The host's side record of a session is deleted when the session is deleted, and its fragments then answer not found.

Layout undo exists only as internal service methods and has no control (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:155). The Go design does not record an operation sequence at all, so there is still no undo of a layout change; the hidden machinery is gone, the user-facing absence stays.
justification: The layout is a short list of tabs in at most two panes. A closed preview is reopened from the tree or its link, and a terminal's tab cannot be lost because it is the host's roster. An undo log for that state would cost more to keep correct than the mistakes it would repair.

reason: A tab's title is captured when the tab opens and does not follow later changes (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:156). A kind's Title function is called on every render with the request's language, so a renamed terminal, a moved file or a language change shows at the next response.

There is no back and forward over visited content; stepping back replays layout operations (packages/client/ui-sidebar-right/README.md:157). The selected side tab of each pane is part of the session page's URL and a selection pushes a history entry, so the browser's Back and Forward step through the content the person visited.

Shell discovery or pseudo-terminal start can fail, and the tab reports the failure without launching another shell (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md:78). Unchanged: the create route's error is shown with its code and a retry, and the shell menu lets the person choose another shell explicitly.
justification: A start can fail for reasons outside the harness (a missing program, a platform without a usable pseudo-terminal). Falling back to a different shell would run the person's commands in a program they did not choose, which is the kind of silent substitution the design forbids elsewhere.

reason: Completion menus and inline suggestions depend on the shell's configuration; the UI adds no completion engine (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md:79). Unchanged: input travels unmodified to the shell.
justification: A terminal's contract is that keys reach the program. A completion engine in the page would have to guess the shell's state and would compete with the shell's own. It is a deliberate non-goal.

reason: Colours a program set through escape sequences are kept by the mounted widget only; a newly opened widget cannot recover them from the host snapshot (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md:80). Unchanged, and more visible: every tab switch or reload draws from a snapshot.
justification: The snapshot is written by the host-side emulator, which belongs to the execution area, and it does not carry program-set palette entries. The browser terminal specification records the same limit and names the terminal area as the place to lift it. Until the snapshot carries them the island restores theme colours only.

reason: Terminal history is bounded, output is not sent to the agent, a tab has no split panes of its own, and processes are not restored after a host restart (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md:81). Unchanged. Two terminals can be shown side by side in the side panel's two panes.
justification: Bounded history is what keeps host memory bounded. A person's terminal producing no model input is a security decision of the remote-surface area. Processes belong to the host process tree and end with it; the surface area records that terminals do not survive a restart, and the roster says so afterwards.

reason: A failed terminal chunk load needs a page reload because React caches a rejected lazy import (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/README.md:82). The terminal is an island: its module is imported when the element appears and again the next time it appears after a failure, and the element shows fallback text meanwhile.

The bullet records that session state dots are drawn by the ui-workspace plugin because the sidebar shell has no notification sources (packages/client/ui-sidebar/README.md:134). It describes which React plugin owns a piece of rendering in the client's slot composition. The Go host renders the whole row, status mark included, in one view from host state, so the division does not exist.

The bullet records that grouping, ordering, search and row state belong to the ui-workspace plugin and not to the sidebar shell (packages/client/ui-sidebar/README.md:135). It is a statement about package boundaries of the client plugin composition, not a limit a user feels. In the Go design one component renders the navigation column.

Copying the local-build version works only with the mouse, because keyboard activation of the brand starts a session (packages/client/ui-sidebar/README.md:136). The version badge is rendered as its own button beside the brand link, so it is reachable by Tab and activated by Enter or Space, and the brand link keeps its own action.

Only wheel and trackpad gestures cross the boundary between the navigation and the session list in one gesture, and the split runs in JavaScript on the main thread without smooth scrolling (packages/client/ui-sidebar/README.md:137). The Go column has one scroller with a sticky toolbar instead of a list scroller nested in a viewport, so every input device scrolls it natively and no script splits a gesture.

Content search is literal token or phrase matching with no fuzzy search, and choosing a result opens the session, not the matching event (packages/client/ui-workspace/README.md:291). Half is removed: a content result links to the session at the matching event's position. Matching is still not fuzzy.
justification: The session-view area keeps the query as one literal phrase by decision, so that search operators typed by a person or a model stay data, and adds a literal substring mode and CJK handling. Fuzzy ranking over transcripts would need a different index; no outcome asks for it.

reason: Sessions can be archived but never deleted, and deleting a workspace registration does not delete its sessions (packages/client/ui-workspace/README.md:292). The Go store can delete a session and the remote surface has an owner-only delete route; the row menu offers Delete behind a confirmation that names what is removed. Removing a workspace still leaves its sessions unless the person asks for the cascade.

A waiting row inside a collapsed group lights no indicator on the group header (packages/client/ui-workspace/README.md:293). The host renders the group header and knows the status of every session in it, so a collapsed group shows a count of sessions that wait for the person, and the header region is replaced when that count changes.

Workspace and search-result rows do not take Tab focus and the tree has no arrow-key navigation (packages/client/ui-workspace/README.md:294). Half is removed: every row is a native link or summary element and is reached by Tab. Arrow-key movement between rows is still missing.
justification: Moving focus with arrow keys needs script (a roving focus), and this area writes none: the first-party script has a fixed list of jobs and a list-navigation behaviour belongs to the design-system area, whose specification is not written. Tab order and the search shortcut reach every row meanwhile.

reason: Under the native composition a remote or in-process browser cannot open a folder dialog, so adding a workspace depends on which picker package was composed (packages/client/ui-workspace/README.md:295). There is one picker, rendered by the host, so adding a workspace works from any browser and does not depend on composition.

The client infers the platform path separator from the home path the host sent and marks the inference as a TODO to be replaced by a host-stamped field (packages/client/ui-directory-picker-browse/src/client/DirectoryBrowser.tsx:124-128). The Go picker never joins or splits a path in the browser: the host renders every entry's absolute path and the breadcrumb with its own path rules, so no separator is inferred anywhere.
